# @vllnt/analytics

> Lightweight, privacy-first analytics with consent management and React integration.

Facts for AI tools. The library has no transport: it queues and gates events, and only
`console.log`s them when `debug: true`. Bring your own backend.

## Package

- npm: `@vllnt/analytics` (MIT), repo: https://github.com/vllnt/analytics
- Ships ESM, CommonJS and type declarations from `dist` (built with tsup)
- Entry points: `@vllnt/analytics` (core + consent + types), `@vllnt/analytics/react` (`AnalyticsProvider`, `useAnalytics`, `useConsent`, `initAnalytics`)
- Peer dependency: React `^18.0.0 || ^19.0.0`
- Install: `pnpm add @vllnt/analytics`

## Behaviour

- Events tracked before `initAnalytics()` are queued and flushed on init.
- Blocked when Do Not Track is on (`"1"` or `"yes"`) or stored consent has `analytics: false`.
- Consent is stored in `localStorage` (`vllnt:analytics-consent`) and a `vllnt-consent` cookie
  (`1` or `0`) for SSR; `getConsentFromCookie(cookieString)` reads it with an anchored match.
- Consent is versioned (`CONSENT_VERSION`); a lower stored version re-prompts.
- `track()` ignores empty or non-string names; `identify()` ignores empty or non-string ids.
- Browser APIs are guarded, so server-side import is safe.

## Develop

Node per `.node-version`, pnpm per `packageManager`:
`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test:coverage && pnpm build`
